title: Webhook delivery: retry transient failures with backoff
description:
Customer webhooks are delivered once and dropped if the receiving server hiccups. Last week a customer's deploy caused 4 minutes of 503s and we lost 312 `invoice.paid` events. Add retries to the delivery worker.

Rules agreed with the integrations team: retry on network timeouts, connection errors and HTTP 5xx only. Never retry on 4xx (the customer has told us the payload is wrong or the endpoint is gone). Maximum 5 attempts in total, with exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s). Log each retry at WARNING with the delivery id. After the last failure mark the delivery `failed`.
comments: integrations-pm: Please do not retry 410 Gone, we auto-disable the endpoint on that.
backend-dev: Delivery id is already in the task kwargs, I will log it.
diff:
diff --git a/notifications/delivery.py b/notifications/delivery.py
--- a/notifications/delivery.py
+++ b/notifications/delivery.py
@@ -1,25 +1,42 @@
 import logging
+import time

 import requests

 log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
+BASE_DELAY = 2
+

 def deliver(delivery_id: str, url: str, payload: dict) -> str:
-    try:
-        resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
-    except requests.RequestException:
-        return "failed"
-    return "delivered" if resp.ok else "failed"
+    delay = BASE_DELAY
+    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
+        try:
+            resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
+            if resp.status_code < 400:
+                return "delivered"
+            if attempt == MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+                return "failed"
+            log.warning("retrying delivery %s after HTTP %s", delivery_id, resp.status_code)
+        except (requests.Timeout, requests.ConnectionError):
+            if attempt == MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+                return "failed"
+            log.warning("retrying delivery %s after network error", delivery_id)
+        time.sleep(delay)
+        delay *= 2
+    return "failed"
